title: Titans' Carnell Tate stuns Cowboys with one of NFL season's strangest touchdowns - CBS Sports
description: The Titans rookie appeared to be down after catching a pass from Cam Ward, but he got b
body:
The Titans rookie appeared to be down after catching a pass from Cam Ward, but he got back up and sprinted to the end zone
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 22, 2026
                            
                    at
    3:32 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            1 min read
            
        
    

            
    
            
        
                
                
                
            
        
            
                    
                Getty Images
            
            

    
        The Dallas Cowboys made a change on defense ahead of their matchup with the Tennessee Titans, stripping defensive coordinator Christian Parker of play-calling duties and handing them to Mike Pettine. The change didn't help Dallas prevent one of the wildest touchdowns you'll see this season, as Titans rookie Carnell Tate broke loose for a 59-yard score on a play where he wasn't touched down. In the third quarter, Cam Ward hit Tate out to the short left on a slant. The rookie wideout went down on his rear end, but got up and ran another 50 yards to the end zone!It looked like Tate was touched down by Cobie Durant, but as it turns out, he got up in time and needed to be tackled. Check out what happened here: 
Perhaps we can't pile on the Cowboys too much for this mistake. It certainly looked like Tate was touched down! Great job by the rookie to finish the play. The Cowboys entered this matchup with the worst defense in the NFL, having allowed 393.8 total yards per game through 10 contests. They are the only team in NFL history to allow 27+ points per game in three straight seasons -- all with different defensive coordinators. 
Tate entered this matchup with 34 receptions for 413 yards and one touchdown through seven games played. He actually missed the last two matchups due to a shoulder injury, but certainly made his presence known in his return to the field on Sunday.

Here are the latest news and rumors from the MLB hot stove on Sunday, Nov. 22

        Welcome to Thanksgiving week. Here in Major League Baseball news, that normally means we're bound for a slow week -- save for a few notable exceptions -- but with the CBA expiring on Dec. 1, we might just be in for a free agent frenzy. Let's hope that's the case. We can start today's set of news and rumors with the biggest free agent out there. Skubal signing to come soon? Tarik Skubal is the No. 1 free agent this offseason and the two-time Cy Young winner appears on pace to make a decision before the CBA expires. Skubal's agent, Scott Boras, hit MLB Network Radio on Sunday and said that there's a "strong likelihood" that a decision comes by that Dec. 1 deadline, especially given that Skubal's signing impacts so many other pitchers (Boras mentioned that it impacts "10-15 pitchers"). The 30-year-old lefty was 12-7 with a 2.72 ERA and 186 strikeouts in 158 ⅔ innings last season, as he bounced back after just six weeks from elbow surgery. The teams most heavily involved in the Skubal rumors to this point have been the Dodgers, Mets, Padres and Blue Jays, all of whom had in-person meetings with him last week.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Tigers sign GilThe Tigers have agreed to a deal with right-hander Luis Gil, per ESPN. It's a one-year, $2.3 million deal.Gil won the American League Rookie of the Year after a productive 2024 season in which he won 15 games and had a 3.50 ERA, but he spent a good portion of 2026 in the minors and was nontendered by the Yankees on Friday. In his limited MLB time last season, Gil had a 4.61 ERA, 1.43 WHIP and 17 strikeouts in 27 ⅓ innings. The Tigers rotation seems set with Framber Valdez, Troy Melton, Keider Montero, Jackson Jobe and River Ryan, so consider Gil a depth option.
The Red Sox also reportedly showed interest.

title: DK Metcalf ejected: Steelers receiver tossed after poking Cooper DeJean in the eye - CBS Sports
description: Metcalf had more penalty than receiving yards against the Eagles
body:
Metcalf had more penalty than receiving yards against the Eagles
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 22, 2026
                            
                    at
    3:29 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            1 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        DK Metcalf's forgettable 2026 season hit a new low during Sunday's game between the Steelers and Eagles. Metcalf was ejected from the game after he appeared to poke Eagles defensive back Cooper DeJean in the eye in the third quarter. It was Metcalf's second unsportsmanlike penalty of the game, which led to his ejection. His first unnecessary roughness penalty occurred early in the third quarter after he got into a shoving match with the Eagles' defense. Metcalf appeared to be frustrated with the Eagles' physicality downfield. Philadelphia's secondary blanketed him on an incomplete pass moments before his altercation with DeJean. 
Metcalf caught just one of four targets for two yards. His only reception occurred on Pittsburgh's first offensive series. 
This has become a history for Metcalf over the years. The eight-year veteran was fined $11,941 by the NFL for taunting following Pittsburgh's Week 4 loss to the Browns. He was suspended for the final two regular-season games of the 2025 season after getting into a physical altercation with a Lions fan, an incident in which Metcalf was sued but ultimately not charged. Metcalf returned for Pittsburgh's AFC wild card game against the Texans, but he had a costly drop early in the game that set the tone for Pittsburgh's 30-6 loss. "They say it's going to a good cause, so I might as well win Walter Payton Man of the Year," Metcalf said this summer when asked if he is tired of giving money to the NFL via fines. "So no, I'm not tired of it."   
A Pro Bowler with Seattle, Metcalf is just two years into a four-year, $132 million contract he signed with the Steelers shortly after Pittsburgh traded for him. Metcalf had just 59 catches for 850 yards and six touchdowns in 2025, a career low in receptions and yardage, plus the second-fewest touchdowns in a season of his career. 2026 has not been much of an improvement, with just 35 catches for 432 yards and two touchdowns this season entering Sunday's game. Metcalf's 12.3 yards per reception, 6.2 yards per target and 40.0% success rate on the year would all be career lows if the season ended today.The Steelers could possibly try to move Metcalf this offseason, but his massive contract will undoubtedly make any trade difficult. In the meantime, the Steelers will continue to try to win games with a subpar receiving corps.

        There's just one week left in the regular season, and it's one of the most fun weeks on the calendar. Some of college football's greatest rivalries will add a new chapter in Week 13, and there are major postseason implications on the line.The weekend gets started early with the Heroes Game between Nebraska and Iowa on Friday. The Hawkeyes are still alive for the Big Ten Championship and a College Football Playoff berth, and they opened as a one-score favorite over the Huskers, who just scored a huge win over Ohio State.Perhaps no game will have a bigger impact on the postseason picture than USC vs. UCLA. The Trojans can get to 9-3 and knock the Bruins out of the Big Ten title game and the College Football Playoff with a win. UCLA is just trying to get to the finish line after losing quarterback Ty Dieffenbach to injury in Saturday's overtime loss to Michigan.In other rivalry games around the country, Alabama is a sizable favorite over Auburn in the Iron Bowl, Ohio State is favored by two scores over Michigan in The Game, and Texas is laying nearly 10 points against Texas A&M.
Here are the opening spreads for each of Week 13's most notable matchups, which include plenty of bitter rivalries.Odds via FanDuel SportsbookThe biggest gamesNebraska at Iowa (-5.5): The Hawkeyes still have everything in front of them between the Big Ten Championship and the College Football Playoff. With the exception of a clunker against Minnesota, Iowa has looked really good this season, particularly on offense. However, the Hawkeyes will have their hands full on Black Friday. Nebraska just upset Ohio State in Lincoln to get the top-25 monkey off its back. The Huskers might be due for a letdown after an emotional win, but maybe their victory over the Buckeyes serves as a springboard. Iowa has won 10 of the last 11 meetings in this series.Texas (-10.5) at Texas A&M: After smashing Arkansas on Saturday, Texas is officially rolling, but that doesn't make Friday night's game any less nerve-wracking. Just remember what happened last season. The third-ranked Aggies went into Austin and suffered an agonizing defeat. Texas A&M would love to repay that favor this week, but the Vegas oddsmakers don't have much confidence, even with the game in Kyle Field. Can the Aggies score enough to put a scare into Texas? That doesn't seem likely given Texas A&M hasn't broken double digits since Oct. 24.
Michigan at Ohio State (-9.5): The Game doesn't have any conference championship or CFP implications, but there are still big stakes. Kyle Whittingham is on the hot seat as a first-year coach, and while beating No. 4 UCLA is a feather in his cap, beating Ohio State in Columbus would be an entire plume. On the other side, Ryan Day has faced plenty of scrutiny as the Buckeyes enter this game with four losses. The Julian Sayin injury has derailed Ohio State's entire season, even though Ohio State remains the most talented team on the field most weeks. Despite how Saturday played out for these teams, Ohio State is a comfortable favorite at home.USC (-7.5) at UCLA: This is an enormous game for both sides. Lincoln Riley has the chance to score another signature win against a beat-up UCLA team. With Ty Dieffenbach getting carted off the field against Michigan, it looks like the Bruins will have to start third-string quarterback Madden Iamaleava against the Trojans. Despite that, USC is only a one-score favorite. That's probably because UCLA has been winning with defense and big plays in high-leverage moments all season. The Bruins must win on the margins once more to remain alive in the CFP race.Auburn at Alabama (-16.5): Anything can happen in the Iron Bowl, and Auburn certainly hopes that's the case this year because the Tigers are massive underdogs as they travel to Bryant-Denny Stadium. Ever since its loss to Tennessee, Alabama has played exceptional football, and it may be headed for a first-round bye in the CFP. That is, of course, assuming that the Crimson Tide handle business on Saturday. Auburn hasn't won the Iron Bowl since 2019, and it hasn't won in Tuscaloosa since 2006.

title: Welcome to Manchester United: Mauricio Pochettino faces grim reality after collapse against Liverpool - CBS Sports
description: A humiliating 4-0 defeat at Liverpool quickly exposed Manchester United's glaring defensive flaws and showed the
body:
A humiliating 4-0 defeat at Liverpool quickly exposed Manchester United's glaring defensive flaws and showed the new manager the massive scale of the rebuild ahead at Old Trafford
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 22, 2026
                            
                    at
    1:59 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            4 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        If he didn't already, Mauricio Pochettino knows what he has gotten himself into now. In his first press conference, the new head coach spoke of leading Manchester United to a "different place."Oh, the places they might go if the first 15 minutes of Pochettino's tenure set the tone for the months ahead. Deepdale, Fratton Park, Ashton Gate. As United's defense buckled under Liverpool's ferocity, you really could convince yourself this was a team that might be at serious risk of relegation, a perpetual-motion machine turning bad vibes into worse performances. Losing to Liverpool away from home isn't a disaster; losing 4-0 after a 15th-minute red card is another matter entirely.The table might have said otherwise, but there was not that much cause for anxiety when Michael Carrick was sacked and Pochettino appointed. For starters, they had appointed a coach with Premier League experience whose least successful postings over his coaching career have been the ones where he has delivered to expectations. That they did not go down the Igor Tudor route was probably enough to ensure United won't risk doing a Spurs.The fixes seemed too straightforward: a better shape out of possession, cutting their diet of spray-and-pray shots. The analytics profile looked perfectly adequate at a stage of the season when expected goals is more predictive than goals and points. United were as near to dead average a Premier League team as you'd find. Eventually this would all have to bottom out.
And then Matthijs de Ligt started playing like a man who hadn't started a Premier League game in a year, moving like Jason Duval on his neighbor's mobility scooter. Leny Yoro made the mistake of a young center back who has been learning all the wrong habits, affording Alexander Isak just enough contact to allow him to go down and earn his team 82 minutes with a man advantage. Giving up a penalty and only getting a yellow might have been the better option for Yoro, even if it had allowed Isak to score another. The path the youngster took looked all the worse when Dominik Szoboszlai larruped in a free kick.When Rio Ngumoha blew past Diogo Dalot and cut back for Florian Wirtz to acrobatically convert, it was game over. There was nothing for Pochettino to instill in this United team, nothing to be done but delay the inevitable shellacking.Perhaps it speaks well of United's new coach that he swiftly understood his initial adjustment to the red card -- Patrick Dorgu dropping back to left back from the wing -- would be insufficient. On came Harry Maguire to marshal a back five. The bleeding was at least stemmed for a while before Ngumoha and Victor Munoz took the scoreline to 4-0 in the final 25 minutes. That that felt like a qualified success says everything about the humiliation United inflict on themselves when they rock up at Anfield.

        
            
                Can Mauricio Pochettino replicate hallmark intensity he brought to USMNT with Manchester United?
                
                    James Benge                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
United may be no wiser as to what Pochettino can do for them, but Pochettino will have a much clearer sense of how little some of these players can do for him. Lisandro Martinez was as cumbersome at left back as he has been in central defense this season, his limbs all at odds with each other as Bradley Barcola rushed by him to square for Ngumoha to score the third. He was not the only one eating dust when Liverpool got running. How could he be? The worst defensive record in Europe's top five leagues has to be a team effort.Youri Tielemans and Kobbie Mainoo are no quicker in a Pochettino midfield than they were in Carrick's. De Ligt is going to need a long run of games to play himself back into form, but even then he does not have the athletic profile for a Premier League defender in the age of verticality. Nor do Dalot, Maguire, Martinez, Yoro, Noussair Mazraoui, Luke Shaw and Ayden Heaven. Perhaps there were moments at Anfield this afternoon where Pochettino found himself longing for Tim Ream, not for his composure and consistency, but for his burst across six yards.He will have to get new defenders in January. Midfielders wouldn't go amiss either, even after all that cash that was splashed on Tielemans, Carlos Baleba and Andrey Santos, who can safely assume he has left Pochettino quite unimpressed given that he was unused when United could really have used a ball-winning midfielder.  "Don't worry about a thing," chanted those hardy few United fans who had waited out the final whistle. Come the end of the season, their optimism will probably be vindicated -- an average team that has appointed an above-average coach should be able to address a position less perilous than it seems. Every little thing should be all right. And yet there is a path ahead of United that really could take them to dark and dangerous places. Pochettino must now steer his club in another direction.

description: Dykes led TCU to the national championship game in his first season, but the results have been uneven in the four
body:
Dykes led TCU to the national championship game in his first season, but the results have been uneven in the four years since
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                            
        
    Nov 22, 2026
                            
                    at
    2:47 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        TCU fired fifth-year coach Sonny Dykes on Sunday after the Horned Frogs' 38-17 loss to Utah, which dropped the team to 5-6 this season. Coming off consecutive 9-4 finishes and four years removed from a CFP National Championship appearance, Dykes and the Horned Frogs never got going offensively this fall after coaching staff changes this offseason."While Sonny's tenure began with the incredible achievement of winning the 2022 Fiesta Bowl and advancing to the national championship game, the proceeding years have seen our program slide further away from that mountain top than can be accepted," TCU athletic director Mike Buddie said in a statement. "I am grateful to Sonny for his belief in TCU, his family's love for the Fort Worth community, and for his coaching staff's commitment to recruiting and developing men of high character."TCU defensive coordinator Andy Avalos will serve as interim coach for Thursday's finale at Texas Tech.Dykes finished 41-23 overall at TCU, including a 26-18 mark against Big 12 competition. His only other losing season came in 2023, one year after the Horned Frogs went 13-2 and lost 65-7 to Georgia in the title game.
TCU trailed by 17 points at intermission during the loss to the Utes before tying the game. However, Utah scored 21 unanswered during a fourth-quarter spurt to win its 11th straight.
        
            
                2026 college football coaching carousel 2026: Tracking hirings and firings
                
                    Brandon Marcello                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
TCU lost its season opener, 15-10, to North Carolina in Ireland on Aug. 29. The Tar Heels aren't yet bowl-eligible under second-year coach Bill Belichick, and the setback sounded alarms in Fort Worth for a program sinking under the current regime.Earlier this month, Dykes said some of the boos heard this season at home and "Fire Sonny" chants were part of the job.
"I didn't notice any of it. I had a job to do, and I was trying to do my job the best that I could. I honestly didn't know about it, didn't see it," Dykes said after a 22-16 win over Kansas. "I think that's part of our job as coaches, is to understand the way things are now. It's very different, it is a different world."The Horned Frogs have alternated wins and losses and, in Big 12 play, suffered a 17-10 defeat at the hands of nationally ranked BYU on Oct. 3. TCU ranks last in the Big 12 in total offense, rushing offense and 15th in scoring offense following play-caller Kendal Briles' departure to South Carolina.Dykes fired co-offensive coordinator and offensive line coach A.J. Ricker in October after a home loss against West Virginia, but the writing was on the wall for his regime.
"TCU's investment in football has led to dramatic growth of our university and city in the past 20 years, and we cannot allow that investment to fall short of its due return, especially at such a pivotal time of change in college sports," Buddie added. "We expect to compete for Big 12 championships, to be a central figure in the College Football Playoff conversation, and our continued investment and growth potential reflects that."Initial candidates at TCUNew Mexico's Jason Eck, TCU defensive coordinator Andy Avalos and LSU defensive coordinator Blake Baker are among the names expected to be in the initial mix, per 247Sports.MORE FROM 247 SPORTS: Live updates on the 2027 coaching carouselEck has the Lobos in the Group of Six playoff conversation this season, while Avalos is a respected assistant within the program. Baker has spent the last couple of years on staff for the Tigers, and his defense this fall has all but carried Lane Kiffin and LSU during his first campaign.

The Bruins' first loss and the Hoosiers' stunning overtime defeat had consequences, as the Longhorns benefited most from the chaos in Week 12

        Six ranked teams lost in the penultimate week of the regular season, and the biggest moves in the newest AP poll came near the top.The Big Ten took the hardest hit: three losses, all to unranked opponents, including two by teams in last week's top six. UCLA is no longer unbeaten after an 18-16 triple-overtime loss at Michigan, a game in which starting quarterback Ty Dieffenbach was carted off in overtime. Indiana lost in overtime at Washington, its first loss to an unranked team in the Curt Cignetti era. Voters dropped both six spots, UCLA to No. 10 and Indiana to No. 12. (The Big Ten Championship scenarios are a mess of possibilities.)Texas cashed in on the Big Ten's misfortunes. The Longhorns jumped three spots to No. 5, leapfrogging UCLA, Indiana and Alabama. Texas was No. 1 in early October before a loss to Oklahoma sent it tumbling. Four weeks ago, it sat at No. 11. The Longhorns close the regular season Friday at Texas A&M.Then there is Ohio State. The preseason No. 1, the same team Texas rallied from 20 points down to beat in Austin, fell nine spots and barely hung on at No. 25 after a 31-28 loss at Nebraska. The Buckeyes finished 17 points ahead of New Mexico, the top team outside the poll, and avoided dropping out of the poll for the first time since 2011. Nebraska snapped a 31-game losing streak against ranked teams, its first such win since 2016, but is the second team left out of the AP's Top 25.
Elsewhere, Missouri stomped No. 17 Kentucky out of the poll and entered at No. 24. body:
Get the latest on the college football coaching carousel as CBS Sports tracks new hires and fires
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                            
        
    Nov 22, 2026
                            
                    at
    2:49 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            4 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        After a few false starts, the coaching carousel finally started spinning in late October. It's not surprising the silly season is off to a slow start after 2025's record-breaking churn. The FBS hired 32 new head coaches, including 17 in the four power conferences, and hundreds more assistant coaches changed jobs. Ninety-three FBS programs have changed coaches over the last three offseasons. The question is whether we've hit a cooling period as schools wrestle with the challenging economics of the NIL and revenue-sharing era.  Maryland kicked off the firing season Oct. 21. More power programs have followed. CBS Sports is tracking every move in the 2026-27 cycle and grading each hire below. 
 Power Four 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Baylor — OUT: Dave Aranda | IN: TBD Dave Aranda won a Big 12 title in 2021 but otherwise led the Bears with middling success over seven seasons. He finished 40-40 and was below .500 in the Big 12 (26-32). Don't be surprised if Baylor seeks an offensive coach, particularly one with strong connections to the Texas high school scene. UTSA's Jeff Traylor, Texas State's GJ Kinne and USC's Lincoln Riley are strong candidates to consider in Waco. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Florida State — OUT: Mike Norvell | IN: TBD After seven whirlwind seasons, which included an undefeated campaign in 2023 while being snubbed from the College Football Playoff, Florida State cut ties with Norvell on Nov. 1 following a loss to Clemson. Is FSU as lucrative a job as it has been in the past? We'll find out as questions arise about the program's financials.  
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Maryland — OUT: Mike Locksley | IN: TBD Maryland kicked off the coaching carousel this year. Mike Locksley is out halfway through his eighth season at Maryland, where he was 39-54 overall. The Terps were 4-8 in back-to-back seasons leading to the decisive 2026. A wide variety of candidates will be considered in College Park. Wake Forest's Jake Dickert, a popular name elsewhere, and Memphis' Charles Huff, a Maryland native, immediately come to mind. Dickert, however, recently signed a new contract with Wake. The Terps have better NIL resources than a year ago, but the job is still difficult in the Big Ten. 

                            
    
                                                
                    
    NC State — OUT: Dave Doeren | IN: Philip Rivers NC State legend Philip Rivers was hired to lead his former program to the mountaintop of the ACC. The legendary NFL quarterback spent six years coaching St. Michael's Catholic High School in Fairhope, Alabama, where he led the program to the playoffs four times. His son, Gunner, is a quarterback committed to NC State. With only a $3.5 million annual salary, NC State is counting on fans and boosters to help fund NIL and secure an elite roster.  Dave Doeren was fired during his 14th season in Raleigh, following a disappointing 31-28 loss at Stanford that dropped the Wolfpack to 1-3 in the ACC. Doeren seemed just good enough to win seven to nine games every year, but disappointing losses always railroaded what could have been special seasons. A downtick in success over the last three years made it clear a change was needed. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    TCU — OUT: Sonny Dykes | IN: TBDFour years after leading TCU to the national championship game, Sonny Dykes is out in Fort Worth. The Horned Frogs simply weren't able to sustain that success, though they did string together nine consecutive wins in 2024 and 2025. In 2026, however, TCU has regressed noticeably with a 5-6 record through 11 games. The Horned Frogs are fielding the 103rd scoring offense in the country, and that side of the ball is supposed to be Dykes' bread and butter.
MORE FROM 247 SPORTS: Live updates on the 2027 coaching carousel Group of Six 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    UTEP — OUT: Scotty Walden | IN: TBD Scotty Walden is out after a 1-9 start in his third season leading UTEP. His tenure produced only six wins across three seasons and the nation's worst-scoring offense in 2026. The Miners' athletics program is among the worst-funded in the country, making this job incredibly challenging. Remember, Walden was coaching at FCS Austin Peay before coming to El Paso, so the list of candidates this time around could be shallow. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Sam Houston — OUT: Phil Longo | IN: TBD Phil Longo didn't last long at Sam Houston. He was fired during his second season after the Bearcats started 1-7. He was only 3-17 with a 1-11 record in Conference USA. The program is not far removed from transitioning from the FCS to the FBS, but it's also only been two years since former coach K.C. Keeler led the Bearcats to a 10-3 record with a win in the New Orleans Bowl. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Arkansas State — OUT: Butch Jones | IN: TBD Butch Jones is out after a 4-6 start to his sixth season at Arkansas State, where he was 30-43 overall. The Red Wolves are aching for a return to their success in the 2010s, when the program rotated through future Power Four coaches Hugh Freeze, Gus Malzahn and Bryan Harsin while recording nine straight winning seasons.
